description_long: AP’s campaign-promise tracker organized pledges across policy areas and assigned status labels to individual items. In the retrieved file, last modified December 3, 2025, the promise to pardon some people convicted or charged in the Jan. 6 attack was marked Kept, with a fulfillment date of January 20, 2025. The promise to close the Department of Education was marked In progress. A separate pledge to cut money to schools with vaccine or mask mandates was marked It’s complicated. The examples show the tracker’s use of different ratings across policy topics, rather than a single overall verdict. AP links the entries to related reporting or source documents, including the presidential action on pardons and its coverage of Trump’s call to withhold school funding. The dataset is not a verified snapshot for March 2026, and these separate AP ratings do not alone prove or disprove a distinct claim that Trump made about uniform success. They support a description of the tracker’s cross-topic status view, while the original title’s claim about a particular fragile success assertion remains unspecified. The linked presidential action confirms the actual clemency date as January 20, 2025; the tracker payload’s contradictory date field is a source-data error.
